hypotheses.description: Improvement-bounty tie-break selectability: ties resolve by _route_tiebreak_key=(hop_count, pool_ids, intermediate_asset, miner_id), whose final component is the submitter-chosen miner_id. _select_winner takes the max improvement, breaking ties by the smallest tiebreak_key, so among equally-good proposals on the same route the winner is whoever chose the lexicographically smallest miner_id — a tie win is costlessly selectable.
hypotheses.key_finding: Through the REAL _route_tiebreak_key + _select_winner (tools/gpu_jobs/improvement_bounty_round_route_v1.py): for equal improvement on the same 2-hop route the tie-break keys differ only in the miner_id slot and the smaller miner_id wins, order-independently. An attacker tying the honest miner's improvement guarantees the win by choosing a smaller miner_id (e.g. '0' < 'honest_miner') costlessly — no bond, extra work, or better proposal. Bounded/non-vacuous: a strictly larger improvement_u64 wins regardless of miner_id (empty-string minimal id at improvement 1000 loses to a large id at 1001), so the lever decides only genuine ties, never a better proposal. The miner_id is a free-form submitter field, not a witness hash or bonded value. Research evidence only; binding the tie-break to a committed/bonded value is an untested design question, not claimed.
